title: Republic of The Gambia
capsule: The Republic of The Gambia is a narrow enclave state surrounding the Gambia River, bounded on three sides by Senegal, established as a British colony and protectorate in the nineteenth century and achieving independence on 18 February 1965 under Prime Minister Dawda Jawara, with full republic status in 1970. Jawara's long rule ended in a bloodless military coup by Yahya Jammeh in July 1994; Jammeh's 22-year authoritarian presidency was marked by severe human rights abuses before he was defeated in the December 2016 election by Adama Barrow and—after an ECOWAS military ultimatum—departed for exile in Equatorial Guinea in January 2017. The country subsequently rejoined the Commonwealth and established a Truth, Reconciliation and Reparations Commission to address Jammeh-era crimes.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Gambia's international boundaries are precisely defined by colonial-era demarcation treaties and are among the most clearly documented in West Africa; the river-corridor shape leaves no ambiguity about territorial extent.
